source: Ministry of Agriculture, Forestry and Fisheries (MAFF), General Directorate of Agriculture, Department of Agricultural Extension — 'បច្ចេកទេសដាំដំណាំឪឡឹក' (Watermelon Cultivation Techniques), 2017.
text:
After plowing, farmers form raised planting beds (ridges). Recommended bed dimensions are: bed width 1 to 1.5 meters, bed height 25 to 30 centimeters, with the furrow/path between beds about 0.5 meters wide and a walking path of about 2 meters left periodically to allow easy access for irrigation, weeding, fertilizing, spraying, and harvesting. Beds are laid out with row spacing (between planting rows/beds) of about 3 meters, and plant (hill) spacing within a row of about 1 meter, with plants set back roughly 0.75 meters from the bed edge in a staggered double-row arrangement.

Basal fertilizer is applied into the planting hole before transplanting or sowing: well-decomposed animal manure or compost, about 1 to 2 kilograms per hill, mixed into the soil in the hole, together with NPK (20-20-15) chemical fertilizer at about 10 grams (roughly one tablespoon) per hill — equivalent to about 3.3 kilograms of NPK 20-20-15 per 500 square meters of planting area, spread along the furrow/bed base. Manure or compost that has not fully decomposed must not be used at planting, because it can burn or kill the young watermelon seedlings.

Applying basal fertilizer at the bottom of the planting hole/bed helps the young plants get a sufficient and even supply of nutrients from the start, producing more vigorous seedlings and stronger vine growth. After placing basal fertilizer, the bed should be irrigated so the fertilizer and soil settle together before planting; this keeps the soil cool for easier seedling establishment and reduces the number of seedlings that wilt or die after transplanting.
